obligations.obligation_text: Be both empathic and confident when pursuing Win/Win outcomes.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Character

obligations.title: Be Considerate, Sensitive, and Brave for Win/Win
obligations.description: Be considerate, sensitive, and brave when pursuing Win/Win outcomes.
obligations.obligation_text: Be considerate, sensitive, and brave when pursuing Win/Win outcomes.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Character

obligations.title: Avoid Borrowing Strength from Position and Power
obligations.description: Avoid borrowing strength from your position, power, credentials, seniority, or affiliations to compensate for lack of internal maturity and emotional strength.
obligations.obligation_text: Avoid borrowing strength from your position, power, credentials, seniority, or affiliations to compensate for lack of internal maturity and emotional strength.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Character

obligations.title: Develop Abundance Mentality as Essential Character Trait for Win/Win
obligations.description: Cultivate an Abundance Mentality—the belief that resources, recognition, and success are not finite or zero-sum—as a foundational character trait for achieving Win/Win outcomes.
obligations.obligation_text: Develop the Abundance Mentality as the third essential character trait for Win/Win, adopting the paradigm that there is plenty out there for everybody.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Character: Develop Abundance Mentality

obligations.title: Associate with Win/Win Models and Mentors
obligations.description: Seek out and spend time with individuals who embody Win/Win thinking to internalize this paradigm through direct exposure and example.
obligations.obligation_text: Associate with a model or mentor who genuinely thinks Win/Win to help develop a Win/Win character, especially if you are deeply scripted in Win/Lose thinking.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Character: Associate with Win/Win Models and Mentors

obligations.title: Read Literature and View Media with Win/Win Models
obligations.description: Consume inspiring literature, films, and plays that present Win/Win role models to expand your exposure to this philosophy in action.
obligations.obligation_text: Read literature and view movies or plays that expose you to models of Win/Win, such as biographies like Anwar Sadat's 'In Search of Identity' and films like 'Chariots of Fire' or plays like 'Les Misérables'.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Character: Read Literature and View Media with Win/Win Models

obligations.title: Search Within Yourself for Validation of Win/Win Principles
obligations.description: Look beyond your conditioned patterns and social scripting to discover authentic validation of Win/Win principles through personal experience and inner reflection.
obligations.obligation_text: Search deeply enough within yourself—beyond scripting, beyond learned attitudes and behaviors—to find the real validation of Win/Win and every other correct principle in your own life.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Character: Search Within Yourself for Validation of Win/Win

obligations.title: Build and Maintain Win/Win Relationships
obligations.description: Establish and sustain relationships grounded in character that support mutual benefit.
obligations.obligation_text: Build and maintain Win/Win relationships from the foundation of character.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Relationships

obligations.title: Make Deposits into the Emotional Bank Account
obligations.description: Build trust in relationships by consistently making deposits into the Emotional Bank Account.
obligations.obligation_text: Make deposits into the Emotional Bank Account to build trust, which is the essence of Win/Win.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Relationships

obligations.title: Put Your Cards on the Table
obligations.description: Be transparent and open in communication when there is mutual trust.
obligations.obligation_text: Put your cards on the table and be open when trust exists in the relationship.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Relationships

obligations.title: Listen with Respect to Different Perspectives
obligations.description: Listen respectfully to others' viewpoints even when you disagree.
obligations.obligation_text: Listen with respect when others describe their perspective, even when you see things differently.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Relationships

obligations.title: Commit to Understand Each Other's Point of View
obligations.description: Make a genuine commitment to deeply understand the other person's perspective.
obligations.obligation_text: Commit to try to deeply understand each other's point of view.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Relationships

obligations.title: Work Together for the Third Alternative
obligations.description: Collaborate to find a synergistic third alternative that benefits both parties.
obligations.obligation_text: Work together for the Third Alternative, the synergistic solution that is better for both parties.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Relationships

obligations.title: Focus on Your Circle of Influence with Win/Lose Individuals
obligations.description: Focus your energy on what you can influence when interacting with Win/Lose individuals.
obligations.obligation_text: When dealing with a person coming from a Win/Lose paradigm, focus on your Circle of Influence.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Relationships

obligations.title: Make Deposits Through Courtesy, Respect, and Appreciation
obligations.description: Build relationship trust by showing genuine courtesy, respect, and appreciation.
obligations.obligation_text: Make deposits into the Emotional Bank Account through genuine courtesy, respect, and appreciation for the other person and their point of view.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Relationships

obligations.title: Stay Longer in the Communication Process
obligations.description: Extend your engagement in communication rather than cutting it short prematurely.
obligations.obligation_text: Stay longer in the communication process when dealing with Win/Lose individuals.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Relationships

obligations.title: Listen More and in Greater Depth
obligations.description: Increase both the quantity and depth of your listening.
obligations.obligation_text: Listen more and listen in greater depth when dealing with Win/Lose individuals.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Relationships

obligations.title: Express Yourself with Greater Courage
obligations.description: Speak up more courageously in difficult interactions.
obligations.obligation_text: Express yourself with greater courage when dealing with Win/Lose individuals.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Relationships

obligations.title: Avoid Being Reactive
obligations.description: Avoid reactive responses in challenging interpersonal situations.
obligations.obligation_text: Do not be reactive when dealing with Win/Lose individuals.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Relationships

obligations.title: Go Deeper Inside Yourself for Strength of Character
obligations.description: Draw on inner character strength to remain proactive in difficult interactions.
obligations.obligation_text: Go deeper inside yourself for strength of character to be proactive when dealing with Win/Lose individuals.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Relationships

obligations.title: Keep Hammering It Out Until the Other Person Realizes Genuine Win/Win Intent
obligations.description: Persist in working through differences until the other party recognizes your genuine commitment to mutual benefit.
obligations.obligation_text: Keep hammering it out until the other person begins to realize that you genuinely want the resolution to be a real win for both of you.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Relationships

obligations.title: Remember That No Deal Is Always an Option
obligations.description: Keep No Deal as a valid alternative when Win/Win cannot be achieved with certain individuals.
obligations.obligation_text: Remember that No Deal is always an option when dealing with those who won't think Win/Win.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Relationships

obligations.title: Occasionally Choose Compromise as Low Form of Win/Win
obligations.description: Accept compromise as an occasional alternative when full Win/Win is not achievable.
obligations.obligation_text: Occasionally choose to go for the low form of Win/Win—compromise—when necessary.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Relationships

obligations.title: Recognize That Not All Decisions Need to Be Win/Win
obligations.description: Accept that some decisions can legitimately be made outside the Win/Win framework.
obligations.obligation_text: Recognize that not all decisions need to be Win/Win, even when the Emotional Bank Account is high.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Relationships

obligations.title: Support Decisions When Emotional Bank Account Is High
obligations.description: Back others' decisions when trust exists in the relationship, even without full involvement or agreement.
obligations.obligation_text: Support decisions made by others when you have a positive Emotional Bank Account, even if you disagree or weren't fully involved.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Relationships

obligations.title: Work to Make Others' Decisions Succeed
obligations.description: Actively invest effort to ensure supported decisions succeed.
obligations.obligation_text: Work to make others' decisions work when you support them.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Relationships

obligations.title: Avoid Being Maliciously Obedient
obligations.description: Avoid passive-aggressive compliance that undermines outcomes while appearing obedient.
obligations.obligation_text: Do not become 'maliciously obedient'—doing exactly and only what you are told while accepting no responsibility for results.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Relationships

obligations.title: Make Five Elements Explicit in Win/Win Agreements
obligations.description: When creating a Win/Win agreement, the practitioner must clearly specify five structural elements: desired results (what is to be done and when), guidelines (parameters and principles), resources (available support), accountability (performance standards and evaluation timing), and consequences (what happens as a result of evaluation).
obligations.obligation_text: In any Win/Win agreement, make the following five elements very explicit: desired results, guidelines, resources, accountability, and consequences.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Agreements: Five Elements of Win/Win Agreements

obligations.title: Identify Desired Results in Win/Win Agreements
obligations.description: Specify the outcomes to be achieved and their timing, focusing on results rather than prescribing the methods by which they will be accomplished.
obligations.obligation_text: Identify desired results (not methods) — what is to be done and when — as the first element of a Win/Win agreement.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Agreements: Desired Results Element

obligations.title: Specify Guidelines in Win/Win Agreements
obligations.description: Define the boundaries, principles, and policies that govern how the desired results should be achieved, providing guardrails without dictating specific methods.
obligations.obligation_text: Specify guidelines — the parameters (principles, policies, etc.) within which results are to be accomplished — as the second element of a Win/Win agreement.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Agreements: Guidelines Element

obligations.title: Identify Resources in Win/Win Agreements
obligations.description: Specify what support will be provided, including human assistance, financial backing, technical tools, and organizational resources available to achieve the agreed-upon results.
obligations.obligation_text: Identify resources — the human, financial, technical, or organizational support available to help accomplish the results — as the third element of a Win/Win agreement.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Agreements: Resources Element

obligations.title: Set Up Accountability in Win/Win Agreements
obligations.description: Establish clear performance standards and schedule specific evaluation times so that all parties know how and when success will be measured.
obligations.obligation_text: Set up accountability — the standards of performance and the time of evaluation — as the fourth element of a Win/Win agreement.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Agreements: Accountability Element

obligations.title: Specify Consequences in Win/Win Agreements
obligations.description: Define what will happen as a result of the evaluation, including both positive and negative outcomes, whether natural or logical consequences, so all parties understand the stakes.
obligations.obligation_text: Specify consequences — good and bad, natural and logical — what does and will happen as a result of the evaluation — as the fifth element of a Win/Win agreement.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Agreements: Consequences Element

obligations.title: Create Clear Mutual Understanding and Agreement Up Front
obligations.description: Establish shared understanding and explicit agreement on all five elements at the beginning of any Win/Win relationship, creating a self-measurement standard for all parties.
obligations.obligation_text: Create a clear mutual understanding and agreement up front in the five areas (desired results, guidelines, resources, accountability, consequences) to establish a standard against which people can measure their own success.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Agreements: Create Mutual Understanding Up Front

obligations.title: Get Out of Their Way When Trust Is High
obligations.description: In a high-trust relationship with a clear Win/Win agreement, the manager or supervisor should step back from direct control and instead serve as a resource for help while receiving accountability reports from the other party.
obligations.obligation_text: When the trust account is high and you have an up-front Win/Win agreement where they know exactly what is expected, get out of their way — your role is to be a source of help and to receive their accountability reports.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Agreements: High Trust Management Approach

obligations.title: Be a Source of Help in High Trust Agreements
obligations.description: In high-trust Win/Win relationships, shift from supervising and controlling to supporting and helping the other party succeed.
obligations.obligation_text: When trust is high and a Win/Win agreement is in place, your role is to be a source of help to the other party.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Agreements: Role in High Trust Culture

obligations.title: Receive Accountability Reports in High Trust Agreements
obligations.description: Accept accountability reports from the other party as the primary means of monitoring progress, rather than engaging in direct surveillance or hovering supervision.
obligations.obligation_text: When trust is high and a Win/Win agreement is in place, receive their accountability reports rather than hovering over or checking up on them.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Agreements: Receive Accountability Reports

obligations.title: Let People Judge Themselves Rather Than Judging Them
obligations.description: Allow individuals to evaluate their own performance against agreed-upon standards rather than imposing external judgment, which both honors their dignity and produces more accurate assessments in high-trust environments.
obligations.obligation_text: Let people judge themselves rather than judging them, as this is much more ennobling to the human spirit and, in a high trust culture, much more accurate.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Agreements: Let People Judge Themselves

obligations.title: Avoid Traditional Authoritarian Supervision
obligations.description: Refrain from using hovering, checking up on, and directing as supervisory methods, as these reflect a Win/Lose mindset and indicate insufficient trust.
obligations.obligation_text: Avoid traditional authoritarian supervision, which is a Win/Lose paradigm and the result of an overdrawn Emotional Bank Account.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Agreements: Avoid Authoritarian Supervision

obligations.title: Avoid Hovering Over and Checking Up on People
obligations.description: Resist the impulse to closely supervise and constantly check on people when trust is low; instead, work on building trust and establishing clear agreements.
obligations.obligation_text: When you don't have trust or a common vision of desired results, avoid the tendency to hover over, check up on, and direct people.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Agreements: Avoid Hovering Supervision

obligations.title: Use Win/Win Agreements to Clarify and Manage Expectations
obligations.description: Employ the five-element Win/Win agreement structure to establish clear expectations in any collaborative or interdependent relationship, whether between employers and employees, project partners, teams, companies and suppliers, or any parties who need to interact to accomplish goals.
obligations.obligation_text: Use Win/Win agreements as an effective way to clarify and manage expectations between people involved in any interdependent endeavor.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Agreements: Use Win/Win Agreements to Clarify Expectations

obligations.title: Focus on Results, Not Methods
obligations.description: In Win/Win performance agreements, shift your paradigm to concentrate on the outcomes to be achieved rather than dictating the specific methods used to achieve them.
obligations.obligation_text: Focus on results rather than methods in Win/Win performance agreements.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Performance Agreements

obligations.title: Let People Evaluate Themselves
obligations.description: In Win/Win agreements, enable people to self-evaluate their performance against criteria they participated in establishing from the beginning.
obligations.obligation_text: Let people evaluate themselves using criteria they helped create up front, rather than playing traditional evaluation games.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Performance Agreements

obligations.title: Create Shared Understanding of Goals Up Front
obligations.description: Establish mutual clarity and agreement on goals from the outset in any collaborative relationship or teaching situation.
obligations.obligation_text: Create a Win/Win shared understanding of the goal at the beginning of any teaching, management, or collaborative endeavor.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Performance Agreements

obligations.title: Communicate Basic Requirements Clearly
obligations.description: Make explicit what is required to achieve different levels of results or performance standards.
obligations.obligation_text: Clearly communicate the basic requirements for different levels of performance or outcomes.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Performance Agreements

obligations.title: Commit to Help Others Succeed
obligations.description: Adopt the mindset and commitment that your role is to support others in achieving their best possible outcomes.
obligations.obligation_text: Commit to helping every person achieve the highest level of success or performance.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Performance Agreements

obligations.title: Let Others Define Their Own Goals
obligations.description: After providing context and requirements, encourage individuals to develop their own personalized goals and approach.
obligations.obligation_text: Invite others to analyze the situation and come up with their own understanding of what they want to accomplish that is unique to them.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Performance Agreements

obligations.title: Meet to Agree on Goals and Plans
obligations.description: Schedule a collaborative session to reach mutual agreement on goals and the specific actions needed to accomplish them.
obligations.obligation_text: Meet together to agree on the desired outcome and the plan to achieve it.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Performance Agreements

obligations.title: Use Manager's Letter for Performance Agreements
obligations.description: Adopt Peter Drucker's recommended practice of documenting performance agreements through a written letter summarizing expectations and plans.
obligations.obligation_text: Use a 'manager's letter' to capture the essence of performance agreements between managers and employees.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Performance Agreements

obligations.title: Hold Deep Discussion Before Manager's Letter
obligations.description: Before documenting a performance agreement, engage in comprehensive dialogue covering expectations, guidelines, and resources to verify alignment with broader organizational objectives.
obligations.obligation_text: Conduct a deep and thorough discussion of expectations, guidelines, and resources to ensure alignment with organizational goals before documenting the agreement.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Performance Agreements

obligations.title: Employee Writes Summary Letter
obligations.description: The employee should document the performance agreement discussion in writing, including the timing of the next review.
obligations.obligation_text: Have the employee write a letter to the manager summarizing the discussion and indicating when the next performance plan or review discussion will take place.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Performance Agreements

obligations.title: Make Win/Win Agreement Central to Management
obligations.description: Treat the creation and maintenance of Win/Win performance agreements as the primary focus of managerial work.
obligations.obligation_text: Make developing Win/Win performance agreements the central activity of management.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Performance Agreements

obligations.title: Let Employees Self-Manage Within Agreement Framework
obligations.description: Once a Win/Win performance agreement is established, step back and let employees direct their own work within the agreed boundaries.
obligations.obligation_text: Allow employees to manage themselves within the framework of the Win/Win agreement once it is in place.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Performance Agreements

obligations.title: Get Out of the Way After Setting Up Agreement
obligations.description: After establishing the Win/Win agreement and getting things started, the manager should step back and not interfere with the employee's self-management.
obligations.obligation_text: Get out of the way after initiating the Win/Win agreement, serving like a pace car that starts things going and then steps aside.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Performance Agreements

obligations.title: Remove Obstacles for Employees
obligations.description: The manager's ongoing role after establishing a Win/Win agreement is to clear barriers and problems that prevent employees from succeeding.
obligations.obligation_text: Focus on removing obstacles ('oil spills') that impede employees' progress within the Win/Win agreement.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Performance Agreements

obligations.title: Become First Assistant to Subordinates
obligations.description: Shift your role from traditional supervisor to being a helper and resource for each subordinate, enabling you to manage more people effectively.
obligations.obligation_text: Become the first assistant to each of your subordinates to greatly increase your span of control.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Performance Agreements

obligations.title: Specify Consequences in Four Areas
obligations.description: In Win/Win agreements, make explicit what the consequences (rewards and penalties) will be across financial, psychological, opportunity, and responsibility dimensions.
obligations.obligation_text: Specify consequences in one or more of four areas: financial, psychic, opportunity, and responsibility.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Performance Agreements

obligations.title: Make Consequences Clear Up Front
obligations.description: Communicate all consequences at the outset of the agreement so there are no surprises and no need for manipulation or game-playing.
obligations.obligation_text: Ensure all people involved know the consequences up front so everything is clear from the beginning.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Performance Agreements

obligations.title: Identify Natural Organizational Consequences
obligations.description: Beyond personal consequences, make explicit the natural organizational outcomes that result from specific behaviors and performance failures.
obligations.obligation_text: Clearly identify what the natural organizational consequences are for behaviors such as being late, refusing to cooperate, not developing Win/Win agreements with subordinates, not holding subordinates accountable, or not promoting their professional growth.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Performance Agreements

obligations.title: Meet Weekly to Evaluate Performance Against Agreement
obligations.description: Parties to a Win/Win agreement should hold a weekly check-in meeting to review performance against the agreement's terms.
obligations.obligation_text: Establish a weekly meeting, typically on a set day such as Sunday afternoon, to evaluate how each party is performing based on the terms of the Win/Win agreement.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Agreements: Weekly Accountability Meetings

obligations.title: Make Consequences Clear in Win/Win Agreements
obligations.description: When creating a Win/Win agreement, make the consequences explicit so all parties know what happens if the agreement is kept or broken.
obligations.obligation_text: Ensure that the consequences of keeping or not keeping the agreement are clearly understood by all parties from the beginning.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Agreements: Make Consequences Clear

obligations.title: Set Clear Expectations from the Beginning
obligations.description: A Win/Win agreement should establish clear expectations for all parties at the outset.
obligations.obligation_text: Establish clear expectations from the beginning on the part of all parties involved in the Win/Win agreement.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Agreements: Set Clear Expectations Up Front

obligations.title: Avoid Hovering Over People or Managing Their Methods
obligations.description: When a Win/Win agreement with accountability is established, the person in authority should not hover over or micromanage the other party's methods.
obligations.obligation_text: Do not hover over people or attempt to manage their methods when a Win/Win agreement with clear accountability is in place.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Agreements: Avoid Hovering and Managing Methods

obligations.title: Avoid Emotional Supervision and Reactive Punishments or Rewards
obligations.description: Avoid emotional over-involvement in supervision and reactive, on-the-spot punishments or rewards when a Win/Win agreement is in place.
obligations.obligation_text: Do not get emotionally strung out trying to supervise every move, and avoid coming up with punishments or rewards on the spot when someone does not do things the way you think they should.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Agreements: Avoid Emotional Supervision and Reactive Punishments

obligations.title: Build Win/Win Agreements on Personal Integrity and Trust
obligations.description: Win/Win agreements must be built on a foundation of personal integrity and trusting relationships, not used as isolated techniques.
obligations.obligation_text: Recognize that Win/Win agreements require personal integrity and a relationship of trust to be maintained; they cannot hold up as isolated techniques.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Agreements: Foundation Requirements

obligations.title: Align Reward Systems with Mission Goals and Values
obligations.description: To achieve mission goals and values, leaders must ensure the organization's reward system is aligned with them.
obligations.obligation_text: Align the reward system with the goals and values in your mission statement if you want to achieve those goals and reflect those values.
obligations.provision_id: Habit 4: Think Win/Win — Systems: Align Reward Systems with Goals and Values

obligations.title: Avoid Talking Win/Win While Rewarding Win/Lose
obligations.description: Leaders must not espouse Win/Win values while their reward systems incentivize Win/Lose behavior.

obligations.obligation_text: Set aspirational OKRs that are uncomfortable and possibly unattainable to push organizations to new heights.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 2 — Dr. Grove's Basic OKR Hygiene

obligations.title: Strive for Achievement Beyond Immediate Grasp
obligations.description: Strive for a level of achievement beyond your immediate grasp to achieve peak performance from yourself and your subordinates.
obligations.obligation_text: Strive for a level of achievement beyond your immediate grasp to achieve peak performance from yourself and your subordinates.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 2 — Dr. Grove's Basic OKR Hygiene

obligations.title: Use OKRs as a Tool, Not a Weapon
obligations.description: Use the OKR system to pace a person and let them gauge their own performance, not as a legal document upon which to base a performance review.
obligations.obligation_text: Use the OKR system to pace a person and let them gauge their own performance, not as a legal document upon which to base a performance review.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 2 — Dr. Grove's Basic OKR Hygiene

obligations.title: Keep OKRs and Bonuses Separate
obligations.description: Keep OKRs and bonuses separate to encourage risk taking and prevent sandbagging.
obligations.obligation_text: Keep OKRs and bonuses separate to encourage risk taking and prevent sandbagging.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 2 — Dr. Grove's Basic OKR Hygiene

obligations.title: Be Patient and Resolute with OKR Adoption
obligations.description: Be patient and resolute; allow an organization up to four or five quarterly cycles to fully embrace the OKR system, and even more to build mature goal muscle.
obligations.obligation_text: Be patient and resolute; allow an organization up to four or five quarterly cycles to fully embrace the OKR system, and even more to build mature goal muscle.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 2 — Dr. Grove's Basic OKR Hygiene

obligations.title: Expect Trial and Error in OKR Process
obligations.description: Expect trial and error in the OKR process; every process requires it.
obligations.obligation_text: Expect trial and error in the OKR process; every process requires it.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 2 — Dr. Grove's Basic OKR Hygiene

obligations.title: Cascade OKRs from Top with Bottom-Up Input
obligations.description: Leaders should drive OKR cascading from the top while actively soliciting and incorporating input from employees at lower levels.
obligations.obligation_text: Cascade OKRs from the top while incorporating input from below.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 2 — Operation Crush Case Study

obligations.title: Allow Operational Details to Flow Upward
obligations.description: Senior leaders should recognize they cannot know all operational details and must enable ideas and solutions to emerge from those closest to the work.
obligations.obligation_text: Allow operational details and implementation ideas to flow upward from frontline employees rather than dictating them from the top.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 2 — Operation Crush Case Study

obligations.title: Avoid Micromanaging Implementation Details
obligations.description: Leaders should set clear goals and problems to solve without micromanaging the specific tools or methods employees use to accomplish them.
obligations.obligation_text: Avoid dictating specific implementation methods to employees; focus on outcomes rather than prescribing exactly how to achieve them.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 2 — Operation Crush Case Study

obligations.title: Use OKRs for Rapid Implementation in Crisis
obligations.description: Deploy OKRs as a management tool to enable swift, coordinated action across the organization when facing urgent challenges.
obligations.obligation_text: Use the OKR system to drive rapid transformation and implementation, especially in crisis situations.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 2 — Operation Crush Case Study

obligations.title: Establish Black-and-White Criteria for Assessment
obligations.description: Create unambiguous, measurable standards for evaluating whether key results have been achieved.
obligations.obligation_text: Establish clear, objective criteria for assessing progress and results on key results.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 2 — Operation Crush Case Study

obligations.title: Translate Generalizations into Actionable Programs
obligations.description: Convert high-level strategic statements into concrete initiatives with clear accountability and coordination.
obligations.obligation_text: Translate broad strategic goals and generalizations into specific, actionable, coordinated programs.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 2 — Operation Crush Case Study

obligations.title: Convert Projects into Company Key Results
obligations.description: Transform significant organizational projects into formal key results that can be tracked and assessed.
obligations.obligation_text: Convert each major project or initiative into a company key result with measurable outcomes.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 2 — Operation Crush Case Study

obligations.title: Communicate Clear Priorities Until Completion
obligations.description: Leaders should clearly articulate the what and why of priorities and sustain focus on them through completion.
obligations.obligation_text: When setting a priority, communicate what must be done, why it must be done, and maintain it as a priority until it is completed.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 2 — Operation Crush Case Study

obligations.title: Identify Top Priorities for the Next Period
obligations.description: Identify what is most important for the next three, six, or twelve months by asking: What are our main priorities for the coming period? Where should people concentrate their efforts?
obligations.obligation_text: Identify what is most important for the next three, six, or twelve months by asking: What are our main priorities for the coming period? Where should people concentrate their efforts?
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Focus on a Handful of Initiatives
obligations.description: Focus on the handful of initiatives that can make a real difference and defer less urgent ones.
obligations.obligation_text: Focus on the handful of initiatives that can make a real difference and defer less urgent ones.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Commit to Chosen Priorities in Word and Deed
obligations.description: Commit to chosen priorities in both word and deed, standing firmly behind a few top-line OKRs.
obligations.obligation_text: Commit to chosen priorities in both word and deed, standing firmly behind a few top-line OKRs.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Start Goal-Setting with Disciplined Thinking at the Top
obligations.description: Start an effective goal-setting system with disciplined thinking at the top, with leaders who invest the time and energy to choose what counts.
obligations.obligation_text: Start an effective goal-setting system with disciplined thinking at the top, with leaders who invest the time and energy to choose what counts.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Pare Back the List of Goals
obligations.description: Pare back the list of goals to a select set, highlighting the vital things that must get done as planned and on time.
obligations.obligation_text: Pare back the list of goals to a select set, highlighting the vital things that must get done as planned and on time.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Senior Leadership Must Personally Commit to OKR Process
obligations.description: For organization-level OKRs, senior leadership must personally commit to the process.
obligations.obligation_text: For organization-level OKRs, senior leadership must personally commit to the process.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Make Public Commitment to OKRs as a Leader
obligations.description: Make a public commitment to OKRs in word and deed as a leader; structured goal setting will not take root by fiat alone.
obligations.obligation_text: Make a public commitment to OKRs in word and deed as a leader; structured goal setting will not take root by fiat alone.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Leaders Must Model OKRs They Set
obligations.description: As a CEO or founder, state clearly what the organization is doing and then model it; if you do not model it, no one else will do it.
obligations.obligation_text: As a CEO or founder, state clearly what the organization is doing and then model it; if you do not model it, no one else will do it.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Communicate Top-Line Goals Clearly Throughout the Organization
obligations.description: Communicate top-line goals clearly throughout the organization for sound decision making, esprit de corps, and superior performance.
obligations.obligation_text: Communicate top-line goals clearly throughout the organization for sound decision making, esprit de corps, and superior performance.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Leaders Need Goals of Their Own
obligations.description: Leaders need to have goals of their own, not just team goals; claiming all goals are team goals is a red flag.
obligations.obligation_text: Leaders need to have goals of their own, not just team goals; claiming all goals are team goals is a red flag.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Leaders Must Communicate the Why Behind Goals
obligations.description: Leaders are required to explain both the reasoning ('why') and the content ('what') of goals, not just milestones, to provide meaning and motivation to their teams.
obligations.obligation_text: Leaders must get across the why as well as the what when communicating goals to their people.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Help People Connect Goals to Mission
obligations.description: Leaders should provide context so employees can see the connection between their personal objectives and the broader organizational purpose.
obligations.obligation_text: Leaders should help their people understand how their individual goals relate to the organization's mission.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Sustain OKR Communication Beyond Initial Rollout
obligations.description: OKR communication is an ongoing process, not a one-time event; leaders must reinforce goals continually rather than just announcing them once.
obligations.obligation_text: Leaders must continue communicating OKRs beyond the initial unveiling at a quarterly all-hands meeting.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Over-Communicate Goals Until People Truly Hear Them
obligations.description: Leaders should persist in communicating goals repeatedly, recognizing that audience comprehension lags behind speaker fatigue.
obligations.obligation_text: Leaders should repeat key messages until they feel tired of saying them, because that is when people are just starting to hear and internalize them.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Frame Objectives with Three to Five Key Results
obligations.description: A well-designed objective should be supported by three to five key results; more than that can dilute focus and obscure progress.
obligations.obligation_text: When an objective is well framed, limit key results to three to five, as this is usually adequate to reach the objective.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Avoid Too Many Key Results
obligations.description: Having excessive key results under one objective undermines the clarity and focus that OKRs are meant to provide.
obligations.obligation_text: Avoid having too many key results for a single objective, as this can dilute focus and obscure progress.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Make Each Key Result Challenging
obligations.description: Key results should stretch the team; if you are certain you will achieve a key result, it is probably not ambitious enough.
obligations.obligation_text: Each key result should be a challenge in its own right, not a certainty.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Push Hard Enough on Key Results
obligations.description: Key results should involve genuine uncertainty; confidence in achievement signals insufficient ambition.
obligations.obligation_text: If you are certain you will achieve a key result, you are probably not pushing hard enough and should set a more ambitious target.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Consider Easing into OKRs Gradually
obligations.description: Organizations new to OKRs should consider a phased implementation approach, as the system represents a significant change to existing processes.
obligations.obligation_text: Since OKRs are a shock to the established order, it may make sense to ease into them gradually rather than implementing all at once.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Consider Starting with Annual OKR Cycle During Transition
obligations.description: An annual cycle can serve as a transitional approach for organizations moving toward more transparent or collaborative goal-setting practices.
obligations.obligation_text: Some companies may begin with an annual OKR cycle as they transition from private to public goal setting, or from a top-down process to a more collaborative one.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Use Dual Cadence with Short and Long-Term OKRs
obligations.description: Best practice suggests running concurrent OKR cycles: shorter-term goals for immediate execution and longer-term goals for strategic alignment.
obligations.obligation_text: Consider using a parallel, dual cadence with short-horizon OKRs supporting annual OKRs and longer-term strategies.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Let Short-Term Goals Drive Actual Work
obligations.description: Short-term OKRs are the engine of execution; they ensure that annual strategic plans translate into actual completed work.
obligations.obligation_text: Keep in mind that shorter-term goals are what drive the actual work and keep annual plans honest and executed.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Use Clear Time Frames and Deadlines
obligations.description: Defined time boundaries and deadlines create urgency and sharpen focus on goal achievement.
obligations.obligation_text: Use clear-cut time frames to intensify focus and commitment; deadlines move us forward.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Adopt Quarterly OKR Cadence for Fast-Changing Markets
obligations.description: For organizations operating in dynamic markets, a three-month OKR cycle provides the right balance of planning horizon and adaptability.
obligations.obligation_text: A quarterly OKR cadence is best suited to keep pace with today's fast-changing markets.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Use Quarterly Cycle to Curb Procrastination
obligations.description: The quarterly time boundary creates urgency that counteracts natural procrastination tendencies and drives measurable performance improvement.
obligations.obligation_text: Use a three-month OKR horizon to curb procrastination and achieve real performance gains.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Set OKRs for Relatively Short Periods for Effective Feedback
obligations.description: Shorter OKR cycles enable timely feedback loops, which are essential for learning and course correction.
obligations.obligation_text: An OKR system should set objectives for a relatively short period so that feedback is received soon after the activity being measured.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Set OKRs at Least Quarterly for Annual Plans
obligations.description: Even with annual strategic planning, OKR cycles should be quarterly or monthly to provide sufficient granularity and feedback frequency.
obligations.obligation_text: If planning on a yearly basis, set OKRs at least as often as quarterly, or perhaps even monthly.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Adapt OKR Cadence to Context and Culture
obligations.description: OKR timing should be customized to the organization's specific circumstances, such as engineering teams using six-week cycles or early-stage companies using monthly cycles.
obligations.obligation_text: Choose the OKR cadence that fits the context and culture of your business; there is no one-size-fits-all approach.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Consider Six-Week OKR Cycles for Engineering Teams
obligations.description: Engineering teams can align OKR cycles with their development sprint cadence, such as six-week intervals.
obligations.obligation_text: An engineering team might opt for six-week OKR cycles to stay in sync with development sprints.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Consider Monthly OKR Cycles for Early-Stage Companies
obligations.description: Startups still searching for product-market fit may benefit from shorter monthly OKR cycles that allow faster iteration.
obligations.obligation_text: A monthly OKR cycle could work for an early-stage company still finding its product-market fit.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Pair Key Results to Measure Both Effect and Counter-Effect
obligations.description: To safeguard quality while pushing for quantitative deliverables, pair key results to measure both effect and counter-effect, as Grove recommended.
obligations.obligation_text: Pair key results to measure both effect and counter-effect in order to safeguard quality while pushing for quantitative deliverables.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Pair Output-Focused Key Results with Quality Counterparts
obligations.description: When key results focus on output, their paired counterparts should stress the quality of the work.
obligations.obligation_text: When key results focus on output, pair them with counterparts that stress the quality of the work.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Remember OKRs Can Be Modified or Scrapped During Cycle
obligations.description: An OKR can be modified or even scrapped at any point in its cycle; they are works in progress, not commandments chiseled in stone.
obligations.obligation_text: Remember that an OKR can be modified or even scrapped at any point in its cycle.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Make Key Results Succinct, Specific, and Measurable
obligations.description: Key results should be succinct, specific, and measurable.
obligations.obligation_text: Make key results succinct, specific, and measurable.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Use a Mix of Outputs and Inputs in Key Results
obligations.description: A mix of outputs and inputs is helpful when setting key results.
obligations.obligation_text: Use a mix of outputs and inputs in key results.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Ensure Key Results Complete the Objective
obligations.description: Completion of all key results must result in attainment of the objective; if not, it is not a valid OKR.
obligations.obligation_text: Ensure that completion of all key results results in attainment of the objective.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Limit Quarterly OKRs to Three to Five
obligations.description: Keep the number of quarterly objectives small—ideally 3 to 5—to maintain focus and avoid overextension.
obligations.obligation_text: Set between three and five quarterly OKRs; avoid adding more objectives as this blurs focus and distracts from what matters most.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Consult with Manager Before Committing to OKRs
obligations.description: Individual contributors should discuss and align their quarterly OKRs with their manager before finalizing them.
obligations.obligation_text: Contributors must consult with their managers before committing to their OKRs for the quarter.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Fit Add-On Objectives into Established Agenda
obligations.description: New goals added mid-quarter must be evaluated against existing commitments and fit within what's already planned.
obligations.obligation_text: Any add-on objectives or key results must fit into the established agenda after quarterly OKRs are committed.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Evaluate New Goals Against Existing Ones
obligations.description: Assess any new objective against current priorities and be willing to remove something before adding.
obligations.obligation_text: When considering a new goal, ask how it stacks up against existing goals and whether something should be dropped to make room for the new commitment.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Keep Number of Objectives Small for Focus
obligations.description: Maintain a small set of objectives to ensure the OKR system delivers its primary benefit: focus.
obligations.obligation_text: Keep the number of objectives small to provide focus in the OKR system.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Have the Discipline to Drop Projects
obligations.description: Be willing to cancel existing projects when necessary, not just start new ones—prioritization requires saying no.
obligations.obligation_text: Have the guts, honesty, and discipline to drop projects as well as to initiate them; say no as well as yes.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Avoid Trying to Focus on Everything
obligations.description: Recognize that spreading attention across too many priorities results in no real focus at all.
obligations.obligation_text: Realize and act on the realization that if you try to focus on everything, you focus on nothing.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Make Top-Line Objectives Significant
obligations.description: Ensure top-line objectives are meaningful and important, not mundane tasks or wish-list items.
obligations.obligation_text: Top-line objectives must be significant—they should merit special attention and move people forward in the here and now.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Do Not Use OKRs as a Catchall Wish List
obligations.description: Treat OKRs as a carefully selected set of high-impact goals, not a comprehensive list of everything the team wants to do.
obligations.obligation_text: OKRs are neither a catchall wish list nor the sum of a team's mundane tasks; they are stringently curated goals.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Link Objectives to Larger Purpose
obligations.description: Connect each objective to the broader mission or purpose the team is meant to advance.
obligations.obligation_text: OKRs should link to the larger purpose the team is expected to deliver around.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Select One to Three High-Leverage Activities
obligations.description: Identify and focus on the small number of activities that will have the greatest impact relative to others.
obligations.obligation_text: Select from many activities of seemingly comparable significance the one, two, or three that provide leverage well beyond the others and concentrate on them.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Put More Wood Behind Fewer Arrows
obligations.description: Focus resources on a small number of high-impact priorities instead of diluting effort across many.
obligations.obligation_text: Concentrate resources and effort on fewer priorities rather than spreading them across many—put more wood behind fewer arrows.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Limit Individual Objectives to Three or Four
obligations.description: Leaders and practitioners should cap their personal objectives at three or four to maintain focus.
obligations.obligation_text: Limit yourself to three or four individual objectives at a time.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Keep Objectives Visible and Accessible
obligations.description: Keep your written objectives physically visible at all times to maintain focus on priorities.
obligations.obligation_text: Print out your objectives and keep them close on your notepad and next to your computer, everywhere you go.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Review Objectives Daily and Ask What Moves the Company Forward
obligations.description: Conduct a daily morning review of your objectives and ask how your actions that day advance organizational goals.
obligations.obligation_text: Each morning, review your objectives and ask yourself what you are doing today to move the company forward.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Be Transparent About Progress and Failures on Objectives
obligations.description: Leaders should openly share their objectives and honestly communicate both progress and failures to their teams.
obligations.obligation_text: Be open about your progress or lack of it; tell your people what you are working on and where you are failing.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Make CEO Priorities Visible for Alignment
obligations.description: In growing companies, leaders must ensure their priorities are visible to enable team alignment.
obligations.obligation_text: As companies scale, make the CEO's priorities visible so people can align for maximum impact.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Show That Mistakes Are Acceptable and Correctable
obligations.description: Leaders should demonstrate that mistakes are acceptable, can be corrected, and should not be feared.
obligations.obligation_text: Show people it is okay to make a mistake, to correct it and move on.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Do Not Fear Making Mistakes
obligations.description: Leaders and practitioners should not let fear of mistakes prevent them from taking action, as fear stifles innovation.
obligations.obligation_text: Do not fear screwing up.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Delegate Tasks to Focus on Big-Picture Objectives
obligations.description: Founders and leaders in growing companies should delegate early-stage responsibilities to focus on strategic priorities.
obligations.obligation_text: At a fast-growing start-up, fire yourself from jobs you did at the beginning; offload tasks to focus on big-picture objectives.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Focus on One Big Thing at a Time
obligations.description: Concentrate on a single major initiative at a time and ensure you have clarity on what that priority is.
obligations.obligation_text: Do only one big thing at a time really well, and know what that one thing is.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Defer Other Things to Meet Time-Bound Objectives
obligations.description: When pursuing objectives with time-bound key results, be prepared to defer or postpone other initiatives.
obligations.obligation_text: To meet an objective with a time-bound key result, defer many other things.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Shelve Features That Do Not Move the Needle
obligations.description: Evaluate whether proposed features will significantly impact key metrics; if not, defer them rather than prioritize them.
obligations.obligation_text: When a feature will not move the needle for user engagement, shelve it rather than make it a top-line priority.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Use OKRs to Enable Bottom-Up Input
obligations.description: Use OKRs as a collaborative framework where leadership sets direction and contributors participate in determining how to achieve goals.
obligations.obligation_text: Use OKRs to move forward in a way that is not all top-down; after leadership sets top objectives, ask contributors how to get there.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Write Down OKRs So Everyone Knows What Others Are Doing
obligations.description: Document OKRs in writing to ensure transparency and eliminate confusion about who is working on what.
obligations.obligation_text: Write down OKRs so everybody knows what everyone else is doing and there is no confusion.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 4 — Focus and Commit to Priorities

obligations.title: Publicly Commit to Objectives
obligations.description: Leaders implementing OKRs are required to make a public commitment to their objectives and maintain that commitment over time.
obligations.obligation_text: Leaders must publicly commit to their objectives and stay steadfast.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 6 — Commit: The Nuna Story

obligations.title: Show Sustained Commitment to Individual OKRs
obligations.description: Individuals at all levels must demonstrate ongoing, sustained commitment to achieving their personal OKRs throughout the cycle.
obligations.obligation_text: Leaders and contributors must show a sustained commitment to reach their own individual OKRs.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 6 — Commit: The Nuna Story

obligations.title: Help Team Commit to Their OKRs
obligations.description: Leaders are responsible for supporting their team members in maintaining sustained commitment to their individual OKRs.
obligations.obligation_text: Leaders must help their team show a sustained commitment to reach their own individual OKRs.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 6 — Commit: The Nuna Story

obligations.title: Commit to the OKR Process Itself
obligations.description: Beyond individual goals, all participants must commit to the OKR methodology and system as an ongoing practice.
obligations.obligation_text: Leaders and contributors must commit to the OKR process itself.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 6 — Commit: The Nuna Story

obligations.title: Build Goal Muscle Gradually
obligations.description: When introducing OKRs, develop your organization's goal-setting capacity step by step rather than attempting too much at once.
obligations.obligation_text: Build your goal muscle gradually, incrementally when implementing OKRs.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 6 — Commit: The Nuna Story

obligations.title: Avoid Doing Too Much Too Soon with OKRs
obligations.description: Do not overload your organization with excessive OKR ambitions at the outset; pace the adoption appropriately.
obligations.obligation_text: Avoid doing too much too soon when implementing OKRs, as it will end in pain.
obligations.provision_id: Chapter 6 — Commit: The Nuna Story

obligations.title: Start OKR Implementation with Leadership Team
obligations.description: Begin the OKR process with executives first before expanding to the broader organization, rather than deploying company-wide immediately.
